title: The Two Ajaxes of Salmydra Bay
world_description:
**The Age of Bronze Ships and Restless Gods.** In the years after a ten-year war has finally ended beneath the walls of Troy, the Aegean is full of weary, quarrelsome victors trying to go home. The sea is no longer a road but a judgment. Storms are read as the moods of gods, wreckage is read as omens, and every harbour is a courtroom where the living argue over who angered heaven.

At the centre of this world lies **Skyra's Reach**, a crescent-shaped harbour on the stony eastern edge of the Greek islands. Its white cliffs hold back the wind, and its black water is so deep that sailors say it has no floor, only a ceiling for the dead. Fishermen's huts and salt-works crowd the shore. Above them climbs a terraced town of limewashed stairs and shrines. At its heart stands the **Hall of Oars**, where captains hang the oars of lost ships as offerings. The oar-rafters creak in every gale like a ribcage.

**The Two Ajaxes.** Two men of that name sailed to Troy, and the harbour remembers both. **Ajax the Great**, son of Telamon, was a towering wall of a man, loyal and grim, who died by his own hand over wounded honour and left a grieving half-brother and a famously unburied pride. **Ajax the Lesser**, son of Oileus, was swift, brilliant with the spear, and fatally arrogant. On the night Troy fell he dragged a priestess from the goddess's altar and so brought the wrath of Athena down on the Greek fleet. Ordinary people confuse the two, and the confusion is itself part of the danger. A prayer to the wrong Ajax goes unheard. An oath sworn in the wrong name can be called back by the dead.

In this world, **the two Ajaxes are not only men but presences.** The Great Ajax lingers as a slow, mournful tide, a pull of heavy water that carries the drowned to quiet shores and shelters those who keep faith. The Lesser Ajax lingers as a squall, a white, shrieking wind that appears in clear skies and wrecks those who have broken sacred law. Every sailor in Skyra's Reach has a story of both. Neither will be mistaken for the other for long.

**The Harbour's Factions.**

The **Keepers of the Oars** are an order of old mariners and widows who tend the Hall, record the names of lost ships and bargain with the sea's silences. They believe the Great Ajax's tide protects the harbour and that its protection can be renewed only by honest offerings. Their leader, the Oarmistress, grows steadily weaker, and no one can agree who will succeed her.

The **House of Oileus** is a band of shipowners, spear-captains and salvagers who claim descent from, or loyalty to, the Lesser Ajax. They are bold, charming and ruthless. They argue that the squall can be bargained with, even ridden, and they have begun trading in **storm-glass**, shards of lightning-fused sand that let a ship summon the white wind for speed or for slaughter. Their wealth is growing, and so are the number of wrecks.

The **Priestesses of the Grey-Eyed Lady** serve a battered shrine on the southern cliff, dedicated to Athena. Many are survivors of the sacked cities, and they remember exactly what was done at the altar. They want justice, not peace, and they hold a sealed record, the **Ledger of Sacrilege**, naming every captain who took part in the desecration of Troy's temples. Some of those captains are now respected men of Skyra's Reach.

The **Salt Ring** is a smugglers' network that runs the coves beneath the cliffs. They trade in everything and favour no god. They hold the one thing every other faction needs: charts of the **Sunken Road**, a drowned causeway on which a ship can cross the dangerous middle sea in days rather than weeks.

**The Voyage.** The central journey is a crossing from Skyra's Reach to **Cape Gyrae**, a razor-backed headland to the west where the Lesser Ajax is said to have died, struck by Poseidon's trident after boasting that he had survived the sea despite the gods. A cenotaph stands there, and beneath it, according to rumour, lies the thing that can reconcile the two Ajaxes or set them against each other for good. The route runs through the **Weeping Shoals**, where the wrecks of a hundred ships lie in clear green water. It then passes the **Isle of Pale Fires**, where dead beacons relight themselves at dusk, and finally the **Gyrae Narrows**, where the Lesser Ajax's squall waits.

A single ship is being fitted out for the crossing: the **Hesperine Gull**, a lean, forty-oared pentekonter rescued from a burned slipway and sheathed in cedar from a half-ruined temple. She needs a crew, a captain's oath and a patron.

**The Central Conflict.** The harbour is dying of a confusion. For a generation the two Ajaxes have been worshipped as one, and the Keepers' calm tide and the House's raging wind have begun to tear against each other above the water. Each year the bay grows more violent, and each year the dead surface in greater numbers, pale and silent, in the shallows. Grain ships no longer dock. The fishermen are starving. If the Ajaxes are not separated, named properly and honoured rightly, Skyra's Reach will be swept into the sea. Yet each faction wants the resolution to favour itself. The Keepers want the Lesser Ajax silenced, the House wants the Great Ajax's tide broken, and the Priestesses want the guilty named before anything is made right.

**Atmosphere.** The world smells of pitch, brine, burned thyme and wet stone. Days are blinding white and nights are loud with the creak of hulls and the faraway cries of gulls that sound too much like voices. Gods are close here, and rarely kind. Every kindness has a price, every oath has a witness in the water, and everyone has a name they would prefer the sea not to remember.

**Stakes.** The harbour has a season, perhaps two, before the next great storm. Choices made on the voyage will decide which Ajax the sea remembers, whether Skyra's Reach is spared, and whether the dead who rise in the shallows are finally allowed to rest.
